metadata.name: COI Legal Risk Knowledge Base
metadata.description: Reference-backed legal and contractual principles used for semantic retrieval and contract-risk analysis.

principles.principle: Where a party refuses to perform, or disables itself from performing, its promise in its entirety, the other party may have a right to put an end to the contract unless it has accepted the contract's continuation.
risk_factors: complete refusal by a contracting party to perform its obligations
conduct that disables a party from performing the contract
continued performance after repudiatory conduct without clearly addressing the consequences
mitigating_factors: clear contractual remedies for material non-performance
termination mechanisms aligned with applicable legal rights
principles.source_section: Section 39 - Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly
principles.analysis_note: Use this principle when assessing clauses dealing with complete refusal, repudiation, or termination arising from fundamental non-performance. It does not establish that every termination clause is high risk.

principles.principle: Failure to perform an obligation at a fixed time may affect whether the contract, or the unperformed part of it, is voidable when the parties intended time to be essential; where time is not essential, delay may instead support a claim for compensation.
risk_factors: strict performance deadlines without clarity on whether time is essential
termination consequences triggered by minor delay
mitigating_factors: reasonable extension or remediation mechanisms where appropriate
principles.source_section: Section 55 - Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential
principles.analysis_note: Use this principle to analyze deadlines, delay, time-is-of-the-essence provisions and termination rights tied to late performance.

principles.principle: A person who rightfully rescinds a contract may be entitled to compensation for damage sustained through the contract's non-fulfilment.
risk_factors: termination provisions that ignore accrued consequences of breach
unclear treatment of losses following rightful rescission
contract language suggesting termination automatically eliminates all accrued remedies
mitigating_factors: clear preservation of accrued rights and remedies
express treatment of outstanding obligations and claims
principles.source_section: Section 75 - Party rightfully rescinding contract, entitled to compensation
principles.analysis_note: Use this principle when assessing consequences-of-termination provisions and whether accrued rights or remedies are addressed.

principles.principle: An indemnity is a contractual undertaking by one party to protect another from loss caused by the promisor's conduct or by the conduct of another person, and the indemnity-holder may have specified rights when acting within the scope of that indemnity.
risk_factors: indemnity obligations extending beyond clearly identified events
unclear boundaries on covered losses or claims
indemnity wording disconnected from the party responsible for the relevant risk
mitigating_factors: scope linked to identified contractual risks
clear treatment of covered damages, costs and proceedings
appropriate financial limits where commercially and legally suitable
principles.source_section: Sections 124 and 125 - Contract of indemnity and rights of indemnity-holder
principles.analysis_note: Sections 124 and 125 establish the statutory framework for indemnity. The listed risk and mitigating factors are analytical considerations derived for contract review and should not be presented as statutory wording.
